label: Likes, interest, confidence
rationale: How you feel about a thing or a plan: you like it, you're into it, you can't wait, you're sure you can do it.
mixUps: English 'interested' and 'confident' are adjectives, but here they are nouns that exist: kyoumi aru, jishin aru (or nai). ki ni itta (I love it) sounds like ki ni natta (it bugged me).

targets.verbSense: enter, go in (an old reading of hairu); the thing gets into your heart
targets.trap: English says 'I love it' in the present, but Japanese says the past, ki ni itta. iru here conjugates like hairu (itta, irimasu), not like iru 'be' (ita, imasu).
targets.use: Nearly always past or -te ru: ki ni itta (I love it, about a gift, purchase or place) and ki ni itteru (I really like it, I've taken to it). The thing you like takes ga or o, and casual speech drops both: kore ki ni itta. Giving a gift: ki ni itte kureru to ii na (I hope you like it).
targets.notes: The negative ki ni iranai (I don't like it) is mostly said about someone's attitude and sounds combative: ano taido ga ki ni iranai. okiniiri means favourite: kore, okiniiri na no.

example.ja: これすごい気に入った！

examplePolite.ja: これ、すごく気に入りました。

targets.verbSense: there is, exist; here you have (an) interest
targets.trap: For 'I'm interested', learners say watashi wa omoshiroi, which means 'I'm funny', or kyoumi desu. Japanese says the interest exists, and the topic takes ni: X ni kyoumi ga aru. X ga omoshiroi (X is interesting) is also fine, but it describes the thing, not you.
targets.use: The topic takes ni, and casual speech often drops ga: X ni kyoumi aru? The blunt reply kyoumi nai (not interested) is very common.
targets.notes: kyoumi o motsu (take an interest in) is the version for an interest someone develops: anime ni kyoumi o motta.

example.english: Are you into anime or anything?

examplePolite.romaji: anime toka ni kyoumi ga arimasu ka?
examplePolite.ja: アニメとかに興味がありますか？
examplePolite.english: Are you interested in anime or anything like that?

targets.verbSense: do, make; with X ni, make something into X (here, a pleasure ahead), not the 'go with' of kore ni suru
targets.trap: English 'look forward to' has no matching verb, and 'I can't wait' as matenai sounds like you've run out of patience. Say tanoshimi ni shiteru or just tanoshimi!; machikirenai (can't wait) is also fine.
targets.use: Nearly always in -te ru for how you feel now: tanoshimi ni shiteru (I'm looking forward to it). The thing takes o, often dropped: ryokou tanoshimi ni shiteru. Polite tanoshimi ni shitemasu closes many messages and plans.
targets.notes: tanoshimi ni shitete ne (look forward to it!) is what you say when you've planned a surprise.

example.romaji: jaa, raishuu tanoshimi ni shiteru ne.
example.ja: じゃあ、来週楽しみにしてるね。
example.english: Okay, looking forward to next week!

examplePolite.romaji: jaa, raishuu tanoshimi ni shitemasu ne.
examplePolite.ja: じゃあ、来週楽しみにしてますね。
examplePolite.english: Well then, I'm looking forward to next week.

targets.verbSense: there is, exist; here you have it (confidence)
targets.trap: 'Confident' is an adjective in English, but Japanese has confidence: jishin aru / jishin nai, and a confident person is jishin aru hito. For 'I'm not sure I can do it', a bare wakaranai sounds like 'I don't know'; say jishin nai, or dekiru ka wakaranai, which is also fine.
targets.use: Heard as often in the negative as the positive, with ga dropped: jishin nai (I'm not sure I can) before a test, an interview or a date. What you're confident in takes ni: ryouri ni wa jishin aru (I'm good at cooking and I know it).
targets.notes: To encourage someone it's motto jishin motte (yo), with motsu, not aru. jishin manman (full of confidence) can sound teasing; the same sound jishin also means earthquake.

example.romaji: ashita no mensetsu, anmari jishin nai na.
example.ja: 明日の面接、あんまり自信ないな。
example.english: I'm not too confident about tomorrow's interview.

examplePolite.romaji: ashita no mensetsu, amari jishin ga nai n desu.
examplePolite.ja: 明日の面接、あまり自信がないんです。
examplePolite.english: I'm not very confident about tomorrow's interview.

reviewPool.english: understand what something means; (negative) make no sense
the light comes on (tsuiteru = is on)
be late for the train (and so miss it)
the last train is gone (no way home)
